sun_heat.title: Severe Heatwave Protocol
sun_heat.desc: Temperature spikes past 38°C in concrete blocks. Mitigate urban heat stress.
sun_heat.scenario: A severe heatwave alert is issued. Your indoor temperature is rising rapidly. What is your immediate tactical action?

options.text: Keep all windows tightly sealed and shut curtains
options.feedback: Incorrect! Sealing traps heat inside. You need cross-ventilation.

options.text: Draw thermal curtains, open windows for cross-breeze, and hydrate
options.feedback: Correct! Blocking direct solar radiation while promoting airflow can help reduce heat stress.

options.text: Turn off all ceiling fans to conserve emergency energy
options.feedback: Incorrect! Fans can assist evaporative cooling on the skin.

mon_flood.title: Monsoon Flash Flood Routing
mon_flood.desc: Torrential downpours trigger sudden water level rises near low-lying canals.
mon_flood.scenario: You are driving near a low-lying underpass as rapid flash floods begin submerging the road. What do you do?

options.text: Drive through quickly before water gets higher
options.feedback: Dangerous! Floodwater can make roads and vehicles unsafe very quickly.

options.text: Abandon vehicle immediately and seek high-ground terrain on foot
options.feedback: Correct! Avoid driving through flooded underpasses and move to safer elevated ground.

options.text: Wait inside the locked car and sleep until help arrives
options.feedback: Risky! Water levels can rise quickly and trap you inside.

tue_haze.title: Transboundary Haze Defense
tue_haze.desc: PSI levels surge into unhealthy brackets due to regional smoke plumes.
tue_haze.scenario: The PSI hits 250 (Very Unhealthy). You need to step outside briefly. What respiratory protection is appropriate?

options.text: Wear a standard surgical paper mask
options.feedback: Incorrect. Surgical masks are not designed to provide the same protection against fine particles as a properly fitted respirator.

options.text: Wear a fitted N95 respirator mask and minimize outdoor exertion
options.feedback: Correct! A properly fitted N95 respirator can reduce exposure to fine particles.

options.text: Cover your mouth with a damp cotton cloth
options.feedback: Incorrect. A damp cloth does not provide reliable protection against fine haze particles.

wed_water.title: PUB Water Disruption Prep
wed_water.desc: Localized pipeline disruption reported. Secure emergency hydration buffers.
wed_water.scenario: A sudden municipal water supply cut is announced for your block. How much emergency water storage should an adult maintain per day?

options.text: 0.5 Liters per day for drinking only
options.feedback: Incorrect. That amount may be insufficient for basic hydration and hygiene needs.

options.text: At least 3 Liters per day for drinking, hygiene, and basic sanitation
options.feedback: Correct! Maintaining an emergency water supply helps provide a basic buffer during disruptions.

options.text: 20 Liters per day for filling bathtubs
options.feedback: Inefficient and unnecessary for a short-term municipal disruption.

thu_supply.title: SCDF Go-Bag Compliance
thu_supply.desc: Audit essential life-support equipment inside emergency deployable storage.
thu_supply.scenario: When packing your emergency Go-Bag for sudden evacuation, which electronic gear is essential?

options.text: High-end gaming laptop and heavy console chargers
options.feedback: Incorrect. These items are bulky and not essential for basic emergency preparedness.

options.text: Power bank, hand-crank emergency radio, and waterproof flashlight
options.feedback: Correct! Reliable communication, backup power and lighting can be useful during disruptions.

options.text: An electric portable fan requiring wall sockets
options.feedback: Incorrect. A wall-powered device may not be useful during a power outage.

fri_comm.title: SGSecure Mesh Comms Drill
fri_comm.desc: Establish alternative offline contact protocols during cellular network disruptions.
fri_comm.scenario: Cellular networks experience complete downtime during a crisis. How should your family sync up?

options.text: Keep calling cellular numbers repeatedly until lines clear
options.feedback: Incorrect. Repeated calls may drain your battery when the network is unavailable.

options.text: Pre-agree on an offline physical rendezvous point and use SMS/mesh apps
options.feedback: Correct! A pre-agreed meeting point provides a clear fallback when normal communication is disrupted.

options.text: Wait indefinitely inside separate shopping malls
options.feedback: Incorrect. A clear communication and meeting plan is safer than leaving arrangements to chance.

sat_blackout.title: Grid-Down Power Contingency
sat_blackout.desc: Manage auxiliary battery assets during island-wide grid failures.
sat_blackout.scenario: An island-wide blackout plunges your apartment into darkness. What is your priority power conservation move?

options.text: Leave all room lights switched on so you notice when power returns
options.feedback: Incorrect. Unnecessary lighting wastes available backup power.

options.text: Unplug sensitive electronics and use low-draw LED lighting/flashlights
options.feedback: Correct! Conserving battery power and protecting sensitive electronics are useful during an outage.

options.text: Light indoor scented candles next to curtains
options.feedback: Dangerous! Open flames near curtains and other materials can create a fire hazard.

floodWarning.question: Heavy rainfall is causing water levels to rise rapidly near your area. What should you do first?

options.a: Move to a safer location and monitor official emergency information.
options.b: Walk toward the flooded area to assess the water depth.
options.c: Wait outside until the situation becomes more serious.
options.d: Drive through the affected area before the road becomes busier.

floodWarning.explanation: When flooding is developing, prioritize personal safety, move away from dangerous areas and follow information from official authorities.

floodWater.question: Floodwater begins entering the ground floor of a building. Which response is most appropriate?

options.a: Move to a safer location using the recommended evacuation route.
options.b: Enter the water to check whether the route is passable.
options.c: Remain beside the entrance and wait for the water to stop.
options.d: Move electrical equipment through the water to protect it.

floodWater.explanation: Floodwater can conceal hazards and create dangerous conditions. Follow evacuation instructions and avoid entering floodwater whenever possible.

evacuation.question: An official evacuation advisory has been issued for your area. What is the appropriate response?

options.a: Prepare essential belongings and follow the recommended evacuation instructions.
options.b: Ignore the advisory until neighbours begin leaving.
options.c: Stay behind to observe the developing situation.
options.d: Choose an unfamiliar shortcut without checking whether it is safe.

evacuation.explanation: Official evacuation instructions should be taken seriously. Prepare essential supplies and use recommended routes or instructions.

weatherAlert.question: Your emergency application displays a severe weather warning. What is the most useful immediate action?

options.a: Check the official warning and prepare according to the identified hazard.
options.b: Disable notifications to avoid unnecessary alerts.
options.c: Continue normal outdoor activities until conditions change.
options.d: Share an unverified warning with everyone immediately.

weatherAlert.explanation: Early warnings are useful when they lead to appropriate preparation. Verify information through official sources before acting on or sharing it.

goBag.question: You have limited time before leaving home. Which item should receive priority?

options.a: Essential medication and other critical personal supplies.
options.d: Heavy items that are difficult to carry.

goBag.explanation: When preparing quickly, prioritize essential personal needs, medication, communication and basic emergency supplies.

communication.question: Your family members are separated when an emergency warning is issued. What should you do?

options.a: Use your agreed communication and rendezvous plan.
options.b: Everyone should independently choose a different location.
options.d: Travel toward the hazard to locate family members.

communication.explanation: A family emergency plan should provide agreed communication methods and meeting arrangements so that people know what to do when normal communication is disrupted.

power.question: A severe weather event causes a temporary power interruption. Which preparation is most useful?

options.a: Keep a flashlight, charged power bank and essential communication devices available.
options.c: Open electrical equipment to inspect it.

power.explanation: Independent lighting and backup power can help maintain basic communication and visibility during a temporary power interruption.

q1.question: What should you do if floodwater is rising around your route?
q1.a: Continue walking through it if the water looks shallow.
q1.b: Move to higher ground and follow official evacuation guidance.
q1.c: Wait in the lowest area until the water stops.

q2.question: Why should you avoid walking through moving floodwater?
q2.a: It can be deeper and stronger than it appears.
q2.b: Moving water is always safe if you walk slowly.
q2.c: It only becomes dangerous at night.

q3.question: What is a safer choice when an evacuation order is issued?
q3.a: Stay home and wait for the water to enter.
q3.b: Follow the recommended evacuation route to safer ground.
q3.c: Take the shortest route through floodwater.

q4.question: What should you do if you see a flooded road?
q4.a: Turn around and use a safer route.
q4.b: Drive through quickly before the water rises.
q4.c: Walk into the water to check its depth.

q5.question: Why is higher ground generally safer during flooding?
q5.a: Floodwater generally collects in lower areas.
q5.b: Higher ground makes floodwater move faster.
q5.c: It guarantees that no flooding can occur.

q6.question: What should you do when authorities provide flood safety instructions?
q6.a: Ignore them if the weather looks clear.
q6.b: Follow the official instructions and evacuation guidance.
q6.c: Wait until other people leave first.

phases.beforeIntro: Small preparations made before an emergency can make it easier to protect yourself and your family when conditions change quickly.
phases.duringIntro: Follow the safest action for the hazard. If there is an immediate threat to life, contact emergency services.
phases.afterIntro: Once the immediate danger has passed, focus on people first, then move carefully towards recovery.

gobag.title: Emergency Go-Bag
gobag.desc: Keep water, medication, first aid supplies, power bank, torch, whistle and important documents ready.

familyPlan.title: Family Emergency Plan
familyPlan.desc: Agree on meeting points, emergency contacts and what to do if family members become separated.

docs.title: Important Documents
docs.desc: Keep identification, medical information, insurance details and emergency contacts accessible.

power.title: Power & Communication
power.desc: Keep phones charged and have backup power available so you can receive emergency updates.

flood.title: Flash Flood
flood.desc: Move to higher ground. Avoid flooded roads, underpasses and underground areas. Never walk or drive through floodwater.

heat.title: Extreme Heat
heat.desc: Drink water regularly, reduce strenuous activity and seek a cool indoor location if you feel unwell.

haze.title: Haze / Poor Air Quality
haze.desc: Monitor air-quality conditions, reduce prolonged outdoor activity and use appropriate respiratory protection when necessary.

weather.title: Severe Weather
weather.desc: Stay indoors when conditions become dangerous and keep away from exposed areas, windows and unsecured objects.

injuries.title: Check for Injuries
injuries.desc: Check yourself and people around you. Call emergency services for serious injuries.

family.title: Account for Family
family.desc: Use your agreed meeting point and contact plan to confirm that family members are safe.

environment.title: Check Your Environment
environment.desc: Do not enter unsafe buildings or areas with standing water, electrical hazards or structural damage.

damage.title: Document Damage
damage.desc: When it is safe, record relevant damage and keep important information for follow-up and recovery.

resources.footer: This hub provides preparedness information and quick access to safety tools. Always follow official emergency instructions during an active incident.

goBagDrill.title: GO-BAG DRILL
goBagDrill.subtitle: Preparedness Packing Drill
goBagDrill.missionBriefText: Build an emergency loadout by selecting equipment for the scenario. Your bag has limited capacity, so prioritise items that support the immediate response.
goBagDrill.rule2: Tap equipment to place it into the go-bag.
goBagDrill.rule3: Keep the loadout within the weight limit.
goBagDrill.rule4: Submit the loadout before the timer expires.
goBagDrill.packInstruction: Tap an equipment card to pack it. Tap again to remove it.
goBagDrill.reviewSubtitle: Review the decisions you made for this emergency scenario.
goBagDrill.essentialIncluded: Essential equipment correctly included in your loadout.
goBagDrill.essentialMissed: This was an essential item for this scenario and was not packed.
goBagDrill.unnecessaryItemsWarning: {{items}} was not a priority for this scenario. Limited bag capacity means unnecessary equipment can crowd out more useful supplies.
goBagDrill.masteredSubtitle: You identified the essential equipment and built an efficient response loadout.
goBagDrill.completeSubtitle: Your preparedness response has been recorded. Review the scenario and try again to improve your result.
goBagDrill.badgeDescription: Completed the scenario without unnecessary equipment.
